whatItIs.text: A tangy-salty-spicy Indian spice blend built on amchoor (dried mango powder), cumin, coriander, dried ginger, and usually black salt — sprinkled over fruit, potatoes, and street snacks.

historyNote.text: Chaat masala is the seasoning of chaat, the Indian street-snack tradition, and every vendor mixes their own; 'fruit chaat masala' variants trade cumin and coriander for more chilli, black salt, and amchoor.

howToChoose.text: Choose blends where amchoor and black salt lead the list, with a bright smell of dried mango and sulphur-tang; small packets from Indian grocers turn over faster and taste fresher.

storage.text: Keep sealed, dark, and dry, replacing it within the year — ground spice fades. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: spice storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Shake it on watermelon, cucumber, boiled eggs, or chips — chaat masala's whole talent is making ordinary things suddenly interesting.
